It is also offered directly to consumers in the UK through Mole Check and General Dermatology services, and deployed in skin cancer pathways in Greece, Romania, and Lithuania via a partnership with Affidea. ## 2) Summary - **Summary:** DERM analyzes dermoscopic images of skin lesions using AI-based algorithms. It returns a suspected diagnosis and referral recommendation to help screen, triage, and assess patients for skin cancer. This helps conserve dermatologist capacity by triaging non-cancerous lesions away from urgent pathways.', "## 3) Intended Use - **Medical Purpose:** DERM is an AI-based skin lesion analysis device intended for the screening, triage, and assessment of skin lesions suspicious for skin cancer, aiming to improve access to assessments and conserve dermatologist capacity. - **Acceptable Input:** Dermoscopic images of cutaneous lesions from patients aged 18 years or over, captured using approved dermoscopic hardware systems. Images should not contain immersion fluid, external objects, or markers. - **Output:** A suspected diagnosis (e.g., possible Melanoma, probable BCC) and, if applicable, a referral recommendation (e.g., 'refer', 'discharge', 'monitor') for the lesion, generated by AI-based algorithms. - **Role in Decision-Making:** DERM functions as an autonomous AI system to make independent clinical decisions for screening, triage, and assessment, issuing management instructions without a second human clinician read. It can also augment other clinical data points to support clinical decision-making. - **Intended Users:** Primary care clinicians (e.g., general practitioners, nurse practitioners) and secondary care clinicians (e.g., dermatologists) who use the outputs for clinical management or decision support. Medical photographers and patients may capture images but are not intended to use the outputs. - **Target Patient Population:** Patients aged 18 years or over with cutaneous lesions suspicious for skin cancer, excluding specific contraindications such as open or ulcerated lesions, lesions obscured by hair/tattoos/scars, or lesions on certain body locations.", '## 5) Mechanism and Development - **Model Type:** Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based algorithms - **Training Data:** DERM has been tested on images of skin lesions that represent the population of patients and lesions it may be used on. These images were collected in powered prospective studies run in the UK, US, and Italy. - **Model Development & Validation:** DERM, a Class III CE-marked AI as a Medical Device, employs AI-based algorithms for skin lesion analysis. It was developed in accordance with Skin Analytics’ ISO 13485:2016 certified Quality Management System and fulfills provisions of UK Medical Device Regulation 2002, EU Medical Device Regulation 2017/745, and New Zealand Medicines Regulations 2003. - **Clinical Trial:** DERM has been tested in powered prospective studies run in the UK, US, and Italy, using images of skin lesions representative of the patient population and lesions for which the device is intended. - **Performance:** DERM demonstrates a 99.9% Negative Predictive Value accuracy rate for ruling out melanoma and performs at or above the level of specialists. It helps avoid urgent suspected cancer referrals for 60-70% of patients in pre-referral sites, with 35-50% being routed towards discharge. In secondary care, it avoids up to 95% of face-to-face USCRs. - **Performance — Negative Predictive Value:** 99.9% (Melanoma) - **Limitations in Evaluating Performance:** The model has been evaluated mostly on Fitzpatrick skin types I-IV, which may limit its generalizability to other skin types.', '## 4) Risks and Limitations - **Known Performance Limitations:** DERM does not provide a definitive diagnosis for skin cancer and should be used with caution on Fitzpatrick skin types V-VI. It does not screen for rare malignant lesions not listed in its outputs (e.g., Merkel Cell Carcinoma). Image quality is critical, and immersion fluid or external objects/markers can adversely impact performance. - **Skin Type Representation & Equity:** DERM has primarily been evaluated on patients with Fitzpatrick skin types I-IV in studies conducted in the UK, US, and Italy, reflecting the prevalence of the disease in the general population.
